title: Smooth video recording and fast automated clip delivery
body:
Create smooth, verifiable clips without computer-use automation. The previous request took 15m30s. Its WebM contains 113 frames across 84.639s of frame timestamps, despite a 129.783s container duration. Transcoding to 30 FPS duplicated frames.

Deliver four child features: timed MCP recording; capture diagnosis and repair; encoding from completed rendered output; deterministic export. MCP control and capture diagnosis can proceed in parallel after agreeing their small shared job contract. Direct-render encoding follows both; deterministic export follows that encoder.

Acceptance:
- Demonstrate a 30-second clip with measured decoded cadence and visible animation advancement.
- Target 35–45 seconds end-to-end for real-time capture on a documented capable host; report measured timing and bottlenecks.
- Preserve the creative session and destination files. No native UI automation or agent-timed stopping.
- Review, performance QA and integration belong to each child, not separate stage tickets.

Planning only: this request creates tickets; implementation awaits authorization.

title: Record timed clips through one MCP call
body:
Let an agent request a clip with destination, duration, FPS and format in one MCP call. Lux owns the timer and returns a job ID, status/progress, cancellation and final output path. Reuse the existing recorder behind a small shared job contract; avoid dialogs, screenshot loops and agent-timed stop calls.

Acceptance:
- Record a 30-second clip without computer-use interaction; target 35–45 seconds total on a documented capable host, measured separately from capture quality.
- Validate format/capabilities and destination; refuse overwrite by default. Cancel/failure cleans temporary output and preserves existing files and the active scene.
- Guard session/scene revision; return actual duration, frame statistics and an explicit quality shortfall rather than false success.
- Reuse the encoder service for supported requested formats; avoid unnecessary transcoding.
- Update and install/check the shipped Lux visual skill.
- Checklist: demonstrate running-app behavior, independent review, relevant checks, commit and merge.

Can proceed alongside capture diagnosis after agreeing the job contract.

title: Diagnose and fix sparse preview recording and incorrect duration
body:
The existing WebM has 113 frames across 84.639s, median frame gap 0.7325s and maximum 1.256s. Its container duration is 129.783s. A 30-FPS MP4 conversion merely duplicates sparse frames.

Instrument completed render, capture, encode and write boundaries. Identify where cadence is lost before selecting a fix. Explicit frame requests are a hypothesis, not a proven remedy. Stop duration measurement at capture end, excluding encoder shutdown and file finalization.

Acceptance:
- Document root cause and a short reproducible diagnostic.
- On a capable host, demonstrate a 30s/30FPS clip with approximately 900 advancing frames; report decoded timestamps, drops, repeats and maximum gaps. Target >=29 actual FPS and <=100ms gaps after startup; detect and report shortfalls.
- Compare visible, occluded and minimized operation, render FPS and recording overhead.
- Validate playback motion and duration, not only headers or a still.
- Checklist: independent review, focused regressions, commit and merge.

References: preview-recorder.ts, visual-worker.mjs, preview-capture-files.ts and webm-duration.ts under apps/studio/src.

title: Encode clips directly from completed rendered frames
body:
Make recording independent of presentation-canvas visibility by feeding completed rendered output to an encoder with explicit timestamps. Use capture-diagnosis evidence to choose the smallest reliable path. Reuse the MCP recording job contract and existing safe file finalization.

Acceptance:
- Select the encoder through measured capability checks; evaluate WebCodecs/hardware or worker/process encoding rather than assuming availability.
- Use bounded buffering, explicit backpressure, cancellation and error propagation. Report dropped frames and quality shortfalls; never mask them by duplication.
- Demonstrate smooth 30s/30FPS output while visible, occluded and minimized on the documented host.
- Measure decoded cadence, render FPS, CPU/GPU cost, memory and total delivery time; compare against baseline.
- Preserve scene state, interactive preview and existing output files.
- Update author-facing tooling documentation if its contract changes.
- Checklist: running-app demonstration, independent review, targeted regressions, commit and merge.

Depends on MCP recording and capture diagnosis; avoid a second parallel recording service.

title: Export deterministic fixed-frame animation clips
body:
Export a saved animation at fixed scene times so complex visuals produce smooth clips even when rendering is slower than real time. This is separate from recording live interactions. Reuse the completed-frame encoder and MCP job service.

Acceptance:
- A 30s/30FPS export renders exactly 900 frames at deterministic simulation times with matching encoded timestamps. Do not skip simulation times or duplicate frames to conceal missed work.
- Snapshot scene, seed, assets/library dependencies and supported saved control animation. Explain unsupported live inputs before starting.
- Isolate export state; preserve the user's current scene, controls and playback.
- Expose progress, cancellation and safe temporary-file finalization through MCP.
- Measure export speed and memory; accept slower-than-real-time operation while reporting an honest estimate.
- Visually inspect motion and decoded cadence; verify repeatability for supported seeded scenes.
- Checklist: running-app demonstration, independent review, relevant regressions, skill documentation/install checks, commit and merge.

Depends on direct completed-frame encoding.
